revisionDesc.change: Vote - Accept-Straight-to-Finalization - The simplest would be to write <:[τ]ο̣ῦ Τούρβωνος το̣[ῦ κα]ὶ̣ <:[ca.8] [γεγυμνασιαρχ]η̣κότος|alt|[ca.12] [ἠγορανομ]η̣κότος:>= - - - || Then: lin4 => [π]όλιν ; lin7 => <#τεσσαράκοντα τρ[ιῶν]=43#>

Vote - ReturnToSender - The readings are convincing, but as [ἠγορανομ]η̣κότος is also possible, I think it is preferable to propose the both possibilities only in the apparatus, not in the transcription.

Submit - Before τοῦ καθʼ Ἡρακλέους at the end of l. 3, η̣κοτος can be read, which, in this context, must be the ending of a participle of a verb expressing tenure of a municipal magistracy. [γεγυμνασιαρχ]η̣κότος is much more frequently attested and thus more likely than [ἠγορανομ]η̣κότος. A former gymnasiarch of the harbour of Heracleopolis is also attested in SPP XX 29v.12 from 227: Πανααιτος γεγυμ(νασιαρχηκότος) τοῦ καθʼ Ἡρακλέους πόλ(ιν) ὅρμου. The descender tilted to the left visible before the papyrus breaks off after Τούρβωνος το̣[ῦ] is probably part of [κα]ὶ̣ (cf. the shape of the iota in καὶ̣ in l. 12). Hence Τούρβωνος το̣[ῦ κα]ὶ̣ [double name] [γεγυμνασιαρχ]η̣κότος.
